items.detail: Every witness verified live on host kara. (1) Receipt: `cat ~/.local/share/uv/tools/get-h3-lore/uv-receipt.toml` -> `requirements = [{ name = "get-h3-lore", git = "https://github.com/get-h3/lore?rev=v0.2.0" }]`; `grep -c 'rev=v0.2.0'` = 1, so it is pinned, not a bare default-branch URL. (2) Exactly one dist-info: `ls -d .../site-packages/*.dist-info | wc -l` = 1 -> `get_h3_lore-0.2.0.dist-info`; `find ~/.local/share/uv/tools/get-h3-lore -name '*0.1.2*'` returned nothing, so the old 0.1.2 dist is gone with no duplicate. (3) `grep -i '^Version:' .../get_h3_lore-0.2.0.dist-info/METADATA` -> `Version: 0.2.0`. (4) Installed `site-packages/lore/__init__.py:3` -> `__version__ = "0.2.0"` (repo lore/__init__.py:3 also 0.2.0). (5) `command -v lore` in a clean login shell (`env -i HOME=/home/kara bash -lc`) -> `/home/kara/.local/bin/lore`, `readlink -f` -> `/home/kara/.local/share/uv/tools/get-h3-lore/bin/lore`, i.e. inside the uv tool install. Caveat investigated and dismissed: the review harness's own PATH prepends `/home/kara/get-h3/lore/.venv/bin`, which shadows the tool install; that entry appears in no shell rc file (`grep -rn 'lore/.venv' ~/.bashrc ~/.profile ~/.bash_profile ~/.zshrc` found nothing) and is absent from the clean login shell, so it is a harness artifact, not a host defect. (6) Three subcommands run live from /tmp in the clean login shell: `lore audit --format json` rc=0 (emits the class registry JSON), `lore match "tests flaked on a stale toolchain on the shared runner"` rc=0, `lore consult "shared runner rebuilt its toolchain mid-wave" --json` rc=0. (7) Evidence: docs/qa/evidence/run-RELEASE-LORE-008/README.md:20 records the exact command `uv tool install --force "git+https://github.com/get-h3/lore@v0.2.0"`; before witnesses at lines 8-16 and after witnesses at lines 36-44; `git show --name-only HEAD` lists exactly that file under commit 3429fbda8eef11dee20d434bc4c8d990c03466dc and `git status --porcelain` on it is empty. The README's residual claim is also accurate: `lore match --json` -> rc=2 `unrecognized arguments: --json`, so the live exercise honestly used flags the installed CLI accepts. Tag resolves as documented: `git rev-parse v0.2.0^{commit}` -> 165cc8f6d354d9ed57d58635c1ad482d0e755cf2. Test suite green: `uv run pytest -x --tb=short` exit_code 0, `572 passed in 8.89s`.
